Make BETTER_AUTH_URL the one explicit production origin for auth, guarded Method requests, and build-time share URLs. Restore the compass icons and update maintained guidance.

findings.title: Local Method guard accepts an unapproved origin
findings.why_it_matters: A local development process configured with a nonlocal BETTER_AUTH_URL will accept that origin for Method POST metadata even though Better Auth rejects the same configuration. For audio requests, this lets a request pass the early metadata guard and reach body parsing before authentication, defeating the plan's single approved local-origin boundary. Restrict configured development origins to localhost:5173 while retaining the explicit test injection seam.
findings.validation_reason: With a nonlocal development BETTER_AUTH_URL such as https://example.test and a matching Origin, shared/app-origin.ts:32 returns that origin for both server/app.ts:157 and agent.ts:626 while auth.ts:61-71 rejects it; the early audio guard at app.ts:156-165 therefore admits a request to parsers/logging despite the single approved local-origin rule, though occurrence in a real dev setup was not measured.

findings.title: Build share URLs can disagree with runtime auth origin
findings.why_it_matters: A production client build without BETTER_AUTH_URL succeeds and writes localhost share URLs when VERCEL is unset, despite the explicit production-origin contract. Even on Vercel, https://localhost passes this build check while configuredAppOrigin rejects the same value at runtime, allowing a successful build whose auth is unavailable. Reusing the runtime validator makes build acceptance and server acceptance agree and limits the local fallback to identified development/test runs.
findings.validation_reason: For a production build with BETTER_AUTH_URL empty and VERCEL unset, vite.config.ts:9 falls back to localhost; with VERCEL=1 and BETTER_AUTH_URL=https://localhost, line 10 accepts the value, yet shared/app-origin.ts:21-24 rejects it for runtime auth, so both reachable configurations can produce a successful build with wrong share URLs or unavailable auth; deployment incidence was not measured.

residual_risks: Build-time and runtime BETTER_AUTH_URL are read at different times; after an environment change without a rebuild, share URLs may be stale. The local package check does not prove deployed runtime configuration.
testing_gaps: server/routes/agent.test.ts:testApp always injects methodRequestOrigin, bypassing the newly changed BETTER_AUTH_URL/environment branch in createAgentRouter. Add an integration case without that override, with VERCEL=1 and misleading NODE_ENV=development, proving missing/malformed/localhost configuration rejects Method POSTs before auth/provider work and an explicit HTTPS configured origin accepts only its exact matching Origin. The shared helper and lazy-auth tests do not prove the router or app-level audio guard actually wires the deployed environment into that policy.
No combined app-level audio and router integration test asserts both reject a disallowed production origin and the superseded request header.
